english.title: Allow another to be in possession of official document or communicate secret code/pass word
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[allowed another, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), to have possession of an official document, namely **(..SPECIFY DOCUMENT..), issued for your use alone]_
(B)_[communicated to **(..SPECIFY TO WHOM WORD WAS COMMUNICATED..) a secret official code word issued for your use alone]_
(C)_[communicated to **(..SPECIFY TO WHOM WORD WAS COMMUNICATED..) a secret official pass word issued for your use alone]_
(D)_[without lawful authority or excuse, had in your possession an official document, namely **(..SPECIFY DOCUMENT..), issued for the use of a person other than yourself]_
(E)_[without lawful authority or excuse, had in your possession a secret official code word issued for the use of a person other than yourself]_
(F)_[without lawful authority or excuse, had in your possession a secret official pass word issued for the use of a person other than yourself]_
(G)_[,on obtaining possession of an official document, namely **(..SPECIFY DOCUMENT..), by finding or otherwise, neglected or failed to restore it to the person or authority by whom or for whose use it was issued or to a police constable]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(2)(b) and 8(2) of the Official Secrets Act 1920.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Whilst this offence is triable either way, it should usually be dealt with on indictment. The offence may only be dealt with summarily with the consent of the Attorney General (section 8(2) Official Secrets Act 1920).
(ii) An official document is a passport or a naval, military, air-force, police, or official pass, permit, certificate, licence or other document of a similar character

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
